principles.title: How I work
principles.subtitle: Four positions I can defend with the code behind them

items.title: Measure, then claim
items.desc: Every projection I made about the WishApply pipeline before it ran was wrong in the same direction. Cost and latency now come from benchmarks that isolate one variable at a time, and from usage events recorded per call.

items.title: Choose the boring mechanism
items.desc: The application loop is an automaton over a finite DOM, not an agent — roughly 7 model calls per job instead of 30–80. A CSS selector that works is more reliable than a model choosing a button.

items.title: Own the whole line
items.desc: Schema and row-level security, payment orchestration, the render service, the deploy. I have shipped products where there was nobody else to hand the hard part to.

items.title: Leave the system readable
items.desc: Architecture documents, a single-baseline migration history, written security audits. The next engineer should be able to disagree with a decision on the merits.

wishapply.name: WishApply
wishapply.summary: Applies to jobs on LinkedIn and Glassdoor: fills the forms, tailors the CV per posting, and answers screening questions from the candidate's own evidence — never from invention.

highlights.lead: An automaton where the DOM is finite.
highlights.text: The application loop is deterministic, so a job costs about 7 model calls instead of the 30–80 an agent would spend deciding each click.

highlights.lead: An agent only where a verifier exists.
highlights.text: CV tailoring loops against a deterministic verifier, which gives it an objective stopping rule — the one place the extra cost pays for itself.

highlights.lead: The cheap model plans, the expensive one writes.
highlights.text: The plan is structured output over a fixed schema and can be audited by reading it; prose quality cannot. The reasoning stage costs about a tenth of the writing.
Claims are graded verified / derived / transferable against an evidence store built with pgvector, so nothing reaches an employer that the candidate's profile does not support.
An undergraduate study measured a 36% drop in average application time, from 12.5 to 8 minutes.

gudi.name: Gudi
gudi.role: Founder & engineer: product, architecture, both apps, backend
gudi.summary: Connects people to nearby cultural events and local sellers. Two applications over one Supabase backend, built from an empty repository.

highlights.text: An Expo app for buyers and a Next.js dashboard for sellers and admins, sharing generated database types through a workspace package so a migration cannot silently break one of them.
Split payments, seller payouts, virtual wallet credits and platform revenue distribution, with webhooks isolated to a service role.
A four-role model expressed as row-level security policies under one naming convention, with security-definer functions instead of ad-hoc checks scattered across clients.

highlights.lead: Built to expand city by city.
highlights.text: PostGIS-backed discovery by location, with multi-tenancy designed as a policy-level change rather than a rewrite.
